concept: Seventeen / a founder origin story for TUESDAY
genre: third-person documentary founder origin story with kinetic captions
why_this_genre: The first three films had no characters: ORRIN and KEEL showed only hands, and Cue used one static talking head as a hook. The Clova reference is a character with an arc, narrated about in the third person over documentary b-roll and big kinetic captions. It is the only inspected genre where a person carries the story.
why_this_routing: Character consistency across shots is the known weakness of text-to-video and was flagged as untested in both earlier loops. The fix is structural, not a prompt trick: shoot one hero character frame with text-to-video, then drive every other character shot from that exact frame with image-to-video, which costs the same $0.10/s at 1080p. Shots where identity does not read - hands, backs, wides, still lifes - stay on cheaper text-to-video.
craft_targets: A character the viewer can follow, which none of the three previous films attempted.
Authored UI carries the plot beats, not just the branding: the dashboards and counters ARE the story, which plays to the one capability measured as strongest across all three loops.
Kinetic captions positioned around the frame, against KEEL's fixed bottom-centre bar.
Over-coverage again: buy ten plates for a film that needs about seven.
character: a woman in her late twenties with deep brown skin, closely cropped natural black hair, small silver stud earrings, wearing a faded olive-green sweatshirt

runs.hypothesis: This plate does double duty: it is the opening shot and it supplies the single reference frame that every later character shot is generated from, so the woman only has to be invented once.

input.prompt: A small dark apartment at night, one lamp off in the corner. A woman in her late twenties with deep brown skin, closely cropped natural black hair, small silver stud earrings, wearing a faded olive-green sweatshirt, sits at a cheap wooden desk lit only by the cold light of her laptop screen. She is framed in a medium shot from slightly off to the side, three-quarters toward camera, her face clearly lit by the screen. She reaches forward and presses one key, then sits back and watches. The camera holds nearly still with the faintest drift in. Shallow depth of field, cold screen light against warm shadow, fine cinematic grain. Clean camera footage with no captions, titles, interface text or graphical text of any kind. No readable words anywhere, and the laptop screen content is not visible.

runs.hypothesis: Faceless hands are Kling's measured strength and carry no identity risk, so this beat needs no reference conditioning.
